description: Hi! We are engineering students passionate about interactive software development, bringing strong technical skills, solid system logic, and a collaborative mindset to the table. We’re currently looking to partner with creative teammates who specialize in animation and game design to help us bring engaging mechanics and fluid visual storytelling into our next project.
summary:
Off-world: An Expedition Journal is a zero-install, 3D web platform that turns historical space hardware into active scientific investigations for learners aged 12–16. Rather than presenting spacecraft as static museum relics, the platform lets students conduct first-person field investigations across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Examining authentic artifacts like the Surveyor 3 camera retrieved by Apollo 12, Curiosity’s landing hardware, and Pioneer 10.

It addresses the challenge by transforming dense, open NASA archives into an interactive, curriculum-aligned inquiry experience. Students analyze ground-truth coordinates, run speed-of-light communication simulations, and collect verified evidence cards in a persistent Space Backpack.

This project is vital because it bridges the middle-school STEM engagement gap, replacing rote memorization with evidence-based deduction. Built with React and Three.js, it runs at 60 FPS on school Chromebooks with zero personal data collection—making authentic space science universally accessible to any classroom.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Off-world: An Expedition Journal is an interactive 3D web platform that transforms NASA's open scientific archives into active field investigations for students aged 12 to 16. Structured as an episodic expedition library, the platform features three core mission volumes:

  • Volume 01 (Moon): Surveyor 3 & Apollo 12 — Investigates solar radiation, lunar dust erosion, and microbial survival on the camera returned by Apollo 12 after two and a half years on the Moon.
  • Volume 02 (Mars): Curiosity at Gale Crater — Forensically analyzes discarded landing hardware (sky crane, heat shield) and geochemical evidence of ancient Martian habitability.
  • Volume 03 (Deep Space): Pioneer 10 Trajectory — Features an interactive speed-of-light propagation simulator calculating real radio signal latency across 8+ billion miles, anchored to final contact.

Students begin in an interactive planetary atlas rendered with authentic NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Viking Mars orbital mosaics. From there, they transition into first-person 3D planetary environments powered by Three.js, walking (WASD) and flying with jetpacks to locate hardware. Approaching equipment and pressing [F] activates an optical inspection HUD that reveals primary engineering data. By solving evidence-based deduction tasks, students unlock persistent, double-sided collectible discovery cards in their digital Space Backpack.

BENEFITS

  • Zero Technical Friction: Runs instantly in any standard browser with no software downloads, app stores, or account creation.
  • Chromebook Optimized: Custom shaders and compressed 3D assets deliver 60 FPS performance on low-spec school hardware.
  • Privacy-Preserving by Design: All progress is stored locally on the client device via localStorage. Zero cookies, tracking, or personal student data (PII) are collected, ensuring full COPPA and FERPA compliance.
  • Universal Accessibility: Features full keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys, Home, End), reduced-motion support, high-contrast typography, and a complete non-WebGL fallback reading mode for low-connectivity environments.

INTENDED IMPACT

Ages 12 to 16 represent the critical window where STEM interest either solidifies or declines due to passive memorization. Off-world replaces rote memorization of launch dates with active scientific deduction. By examining how rocket exhaust sandblasted Surveyor 3's chassis or why Curiosity's landing debris was jettisoned away from pristine soil sampling zones, students learn to think like NASA mission scientists. The platform unites orbital mechanics, materials science, planetary geology, and robotics into one cohesive learning experience.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & HARDWARE

  • Frontend & Core: TypeScript, React 18, Vite, Node.js.
  • 3D & Graphics: Three.js, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, Google Draco geometry decoders, custom GLSL cel-shading shaders.
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS, PostCSS, Lucide React icons, self-hosted web fonts.
  • Verification & Testing: Custom automated test suite (scripts/check-expedition.mjs) verifying 13 missions, 52 primary discoveries, telemetry mathematics, and versioned data migrations.
  • Target Hardware: Standard desktop computers, school Chromebooks, and laptops.

HOW THE PROJECT IS CREATIVE

  • Hardware as Living Evidence: Instead of portraying retired spacecraft as static museum pieces or space debris, we treat every probe left behind as an ongoing experiment that continues to teach us about space environments over decades.
  • Graphic Novel Aesthetic Meets Planetary Science: We merged an illustrated, cel-shaded expedition journal with authentic scientific documentation, avoiding both dry technical spreadsheets and unrealistic arcade mechanics.
  • Space Backpack Progression: Replaces arbitrary gaming badges with authentic scientific literacy, rewarding learners with verified discovery dossiers citing primary NASA research.

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM

  • The Classroom Digital Divide: We chose lightweight Three.js over heavy game engines to ensure seamless operation on low-bandwidth school networks.
  • Scientific Integrity: Every discovery explicitly cites and links to primary NASA open data, including NASA NTRS Technical Reports (NASA-CR-121796 and NTRS 20130010911), NASA SVS elevation maps (SVS #4720), NASA PDS DE421 landing coordinates, and JPL Deep Space Network telemetry.
  • Accessibility & Cognitive Load: We ensured all essential content is accessible without 3D mouse dexterity or audio cues, breaking complex aerospace papers into digestible, inquiry-driven milestones.
What We Would Build Next (Roadmap)
  • Real Elevation Data: Stream NASA Trek and USGS digital elevation models (DEMs) directly into real-scale 3D terrain meshes.
  • Live Orbital Ephemerides: Connect to the NASA JPL Horizons API for dynamic flyby vectors and real-time spacecraft positioning.
  • WebXR Support: Add native VR and AR modes for hands-on spatial inspection in classrooms using headsets (Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro).
  • Educator Dashboard: Introduce guided classroom sessions, printable mission worksheets, and curriculum-aligned quizzes.
  • Community Mission Studio: Provide a web-based editor for students and teachers to build custom missions using any public NASA 3D asset and archive record.
